messages:
Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — ran a seq/batch sweep across A100 / H100 / L40S with three kernel configs: flash2-opt, paged-kv, fused-attn-concat. Saw a sharp latency step on H100 when batch=8 and seq>=4096, and KV-cache eviction looks suspiciously correlated. Attaching perf-bot summary below. :eyes:

Ajay Patel: Can you paste the exact configs and the perf summary? wondering if batching heuristics flipped or kernel-selection fallback triggered. :thinking:

Maria Chen: Perf run command: `./bench_attn --gpus H100,A100,L40S --seq-sweep 512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384 --batch-sweep 1,2,4,8,16 --kernels flash2-opt,paged-kv,fused-attn-concat --kv-size 6GB`

Kenji Saito: Pasted a cropped profiler log — kernel selection + KV events (timestamps are local):
```
[14:11:02] device=H100 kernel=flash2-opt selected seq=2048 batch=4 throughput=12.4k tok/s latency=18.3ms
[14:11:07] device=H100 kernel=flash2-opt selected seq=4096 batch=4 throughput=9.8k tok/s latency=24.7ms
[14:11:11] device=H100 kernel=paged-kv fallback seq=4096 batch=8 kv_spill=true kv_evict_mb=1024 memcpy_ms=12.1 latency=59.9ms
[14:12:05] device=A100 kernel=paged-kv seq=8192 batch=2 kv_spill=true kv_evict_mb=2048 memcpy_ms=34.4 latency=95ms
[14:12:40] device=L40S kernel=fused-attn-concat seq=16384 batch=1 kv_cache_ok=false latency=310ms
```

Kenji Saito: Short take — on H100 we hit a config where flash2-opt was still chosen for seq=4096 but when batch jumped to 8 the runtime decided paged-kv (fallback) and we observed a big memcpy spike during KV eviction. The memcpy_ms ~12ms explains the ~2-3x latency jump.

perf-bot: AUTOMATED SUMMARY: runs=36, anomalies=3
- H100: batch>=8 & seq>=4096 -> latency +1.9x vs baseline (likely KV eviction + kernel fallback)
- A100: seq>=8192 -> consistent kv_spill events, higher memcpy overhead
- L40S: seq>16384 -> fused-attn-concat shows stability issues (OOM fallback triggered in 2 runs)
RECOMMENDATIONS: consider pinning flash2-opt for H100 when seq<=2048; enable proactive KV prefetch/spill throttle; tweak batching heuristics to avoid batch=8 at mid-large seqs.

Maria Chen: Thanks. @Ajay can you run a focused nvprof on H100 for seq=4096 batch=8 (flash2-opt forced vs auto) and upload flamegraphs? I want to see memcpy vs kernel time split. :rocket:

Ajay Patel: Yep will run now. nvprof + Nsight timeline w/ `--trace-memory` and `--trace-api` set. Command I'm about to run: `./bench_attn --device H100 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kernel auto && ./bench_attn --device H100 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --kernel flash2-opt`

Ajay Patel: Quick note — if KV eviction is moving ~1GB chunks, the memcpy stalls will dominate at these batch sizes because concurrency drops (less overlap).

Kenji Saito: I uploaded a tiny flamegraph gist: https://gist.github.com/ksaito/fflame-177555 (shows memcpy spikes aligned with `kv_evict()` calls). Also, fused-attn-concat reduced memcpy but increased kernel launch count (more small kernels) so overall latency sometimes worse at high seq due to launch overhead.

Maria Chen: Good catch. So two levers: 1) avoid config that forces kv_evict frequently (batching heuristics / batch cap), 2) prefer kernels that reduce memcpy at the cost of kernel launches for some ranges. We should add a quick decision rule in kernel selector: if predicted kv_active_bytes > 3GB and batch>=8, prefer paged-kv with staggered eviction OR throttle batch size.

perf-bot: CI test `attn-sweep-h100-kv-throttle` queued with patch suggestion. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/attn/177555/

Ajay Patel: Running nvprof now, will share traces + a short summary in this thread when done. If we agree on a heuristic tweak I'll open a tiny PR to add a guard in selector.

Maria Chen: Sounds good. If nvprof confirms memcpy stall, we'll push a conservative batching cap for next canary. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
